raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Batched generation with per-prompt `session_params` currently forwards the entire list to each request, where the tokenizer manager expects one dictionary. Normalize the metadata against the original batch before parallel sampling, then give each prompt its own session dictionary. Its `n > 1` children retain that same dictionary.

Scalar dictionaries remain shared metadata; singleton lists for scalar requests normalize to a dictionary. Empty or malformed lists and wrong batch cardinality fail before fan-out. Empty-token session continuation preserves the same behavior for a dictionary and its singleton-list equivalent.

Builds on #27257 and the validation-boundary analysis from [he-yufeng](https://github.com/he-yufeng) and [chengcuiping](https://github.com/chengcuiping). Fixes #27218.

## Validation

`test_io_struct.py` and `test_tokenizer_manager_session_params.py`: **60 passed, 2 CUDA tests skipped** on CPU. The regression drives the real asynchronous tokenizer-manager fan-out and checks both prefix warm-up and the six prompt-major children of a two-prompt `n = 3` request. Request-normalization tests also cover invalid lists and empty-token continuation. No GPU runtime claim is made.

All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Code formatting and style checks.
- [x] Unit regression coverage.
- [x] Documentation: No new API; session normalization behavior described above.
- [x] Model accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable to this parsing/request-normalization fix.

## Code Review

This pull request updates `GenerateReqInput.__getitem__` to support list-valued `session_params` by indexing them per subrequest, and adds corresponding unit tests. The reviewer identified a potential `IndexError` when parallel sampling (`n > 1`) is used because the batch size expands while `session_params` does not. They suggested using modulo indexing to safely map expanded sub-requests and adding a test case to cover this scenario.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

If parallel sampling is used (e.g., `n > 1`), the batch is expanded to a larger size `num = batch_size * parallel_sample_num`. However, `self.session_params` is not expanded in `_normalize_batch_inputs`. As a result, accessing `self.session_params[i]` for `i >= batch_size` will raise an `IndexError`.

Using modulo indexing `i % len(self.session_params)` safely maps the expanded sub-request back to its corresponding original session parameter, preventing the `IndexError` and correctly supporting parallel sampling.

            session_params=(
                self.session_params[i % len(self.session_params)]
                if isinstance(self.session_params, list) and self.session_params
                else self.session_params
            ),

    def test_getitem_session_params_per_sample(self):

        scalar dict is forwarded whole."""
        req = GenerateReqInput(
            text=["Hello", "World"],
            sampling_params=[{}, {}],
            rid=["id1", "id2"],
            session_params=[{"id": "s1"}, {"id": "s2"}],
        )
        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
        self.assertEqual(req[0].session_params, {"id": "s1"})
        self.assertEqual(req[1].session_params, {"id": "s2"})

        req = GenerateReqInput(
            text=["Hello", "World"],
            sampling_params=[{}, {}],
            rid=["id1", "id2"],
            session_params={"id": "shared"},
        )
        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
        self.assertEqual(req[0].session_params, {"id": "shared"})
        self.assertEqual(req[1].session_params, {"id": "shared"})

        # Test with parallel sampling (n > 1) where batch is expanded
        req = GenerateReqInput(
            text=["Hello", "World"],
            sampling_params={"n": 2},
            rid=["id1", "id2"],
            session_params=[{"id": "s1"}, {"id": "s2"}],
        )
        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
        self.assertEqual(req[0].session_params, {"id": "s1"})
        self.assertEqual(req[1].session_params, {"id": "s2"})
        self.assertEqual(req[2].session_params, {"id": "s1"})
        self.assertEqual(req[3].session_params, {"id": "s2"})

+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import GenerateReqInput  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.managers.tokenizer_manager import TokenizerManager  # noqa: E402
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=3, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestTokenizerManagerSessionParams(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
+    async def test_parallel_sampling_preserves_per_prompt_session_params(self):
+        batch = GenerateReqInput(
+            text=["first", "second"],
+            rid=["prompt-1", "prompt-2"],
+            sampling_params={"n": 3},
+            session_params=[{"id": "s1"}, {"id": "s2"}],
+        )
+        batch.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+
+        manager = object.__new__(TokenizerManager)
+        manager.rid_to_state = {
+            rid: SimpleNamespace(
+                time_stats=SimpleNamespace(set_finished_time=lambda: None)
+            )
+            for rid in batch.rid
+        }
+
+        async def tokenize(request):
+            return SimpleNamespace(
+                rid=request.rid,
+                input_ids=[],
+                mm_inputs=None,
+                sampling_params=SimpleNamespace(max_new_tokens=16),
+                session_params=request.session_params,
+            )
+
+        sent = []
+
+        async def send_one_request(request):
+            sent.append(request)
+
+        def init_state(request):
+            manager.rid_to_state[request.rid] = SimpleNamespace(
+                time_stats=SimpleNamespace()
+            )
+
+        async def wait_one_response(_request, _http_request):
+            yield {}
+
+        async def collect_batch_responses(_generators):
+            return []
+
+        manager._tokenize_one_request = tokenize
+        manager._init_req_state = init_state
+        manager._send_one_request = send_one_request
+        manager._wait_one_response = wait_one_response
+        manager._collect_batch_responses = collect_batch_responses
+
+        outputs = [output async for output in manager._handle_batch_request(batch)]
+
+        self.assertEqual(outputs, [[]])
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [request.session_params for request in sent[:2]],
+            [{"id": "s1"}, {"id": "s2"}],
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [request.session_params for request in sent[2:]],
+            [
+                {"id": "s1"},
+                {"id": "s1"},
+                {"id": "s1"},
+                {"id": "s2"},
+                {"id": "s2"},
+                {"id": "s2"},
+            ],
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

## Code Review

This pull request updates `GenerateReqInput.__getitem__` to support list-valued `session_params` by indexing them per subrequest, and adds corresponding unit tests. The reviewer identified a potential `IndexError` when parallel sampling (`n > 1`) is used because the batch size expands while `session_params` does not. They suggested using modulo indexing to safely map expanded sub-requests and adding a test case to cover this scenario.
